summary: #2335 meets F258's E2. On a fired run-time check the stage is dropped, dependents wait and the next refresh resumes from the sink. That is the held state users and the pipeline see: `held`, exit 8, nothing committed, the same batch next time. A fired check holds whatever `on_violation` says, because there are no rows to quarantine.
note: A failed condition raises `Held` before anything is applied and keeps its stage. A fired check raises part-way through the plan, so rebuilding the stage from the sink avoids applying part of a batch twice. Conditions: T1, the sink's version and the quarantine table are unchanged after a fired check. T2, a later refresh over a batch that no longer fires commits it, and the sink equals a fresh full run. T3, independent nodes in the same refresh still commit. `docs/how-to-quarantine.md` says so in one sentence. Amended 2026-11-22 by the maintainer's renumbering of exit codes by severity (#2458): a held node now exits 7.
